## Purpose

Make HiSparse work, and pay off, on GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`). Fixes #59176.

Flash is the first hybrid model on HiSparse (11 of 45 layers sparse MLA, the rest KDA). It hit startup failures, serving bugs, and a device layout that used *more* GPU memory per request than no HiSparse.

## Changes

**Startup**
- Read `index_topk` from `hf_text_config`, because Flash's top-level config is multimodal.
- `resolve_hisparse_specs` groups only the MLA specs. The KDA and tail-ring groups need the KV layout, which isn't resolved yet at that point.

**Serving**
- Skip per-layer host mirrors outside connector steps. CUDA graph capture raised "HiSparse layer 0 mirrored twice" and startup hung.
- **Core, one line (`gpu/model_runner.py`):** pass `attn_metadata` to `kv_connector.pre_forward` on PIECEWISE and eager steps, as FULL steps already do.
  - Under breakable CUDA graphs (the default for Flash), PIECEWISE replay skips Flash's in-layer HiSparse prepare, which lives in the captured KV-update op.
  - With host-resident pages, the swap-row counter then overflows. This reproduces on B200 with the line reverted.
  - Other connectors ignore the kwarg.
- The kpool indexer places the tail right after the selected pools. This leaves no `-1` gaps in top-k rows, which `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` read as pages and crashed on (Hopper).
- Backends declare `supports_hisparse()`, and selection with HiSparse on skips sparse-MLA backends without a HiSparse path. On Hopper, FlashInfer SM90 read stale KV on prefix hits, and GSM8K fell from 0.901 to 0.745. SM90 support is #61277.

**Device layout** (`vllm/v1/hisparse/`). Every pool block is the size of the largest page, which on Flash is a ~1.1 MB KDA group.
- Hot/resident groups pack up to that page instead of the indexer page, going from 22 groups to 4.
- The indexer block fills that page with whole 256-token kernel pages: 12 on Flash, instead of one 128-token block.
  - The prefix-cache hash block is unchanged.
- KDA (align-mode Mamba) blocks take the indexer kernel page (256 tokens) instead of the hybrid attention block, which HiSparse groups don't use (`_align_hybrid_block_size`).
  - Otherwise multi-page indexer blocks would grow the scheduler block to 9216 tokens (bf16) and 47872 (fp8).
  - It is now the indexer block: 3072 and 2816 tokens, vs 2304 and 4352 before this PR. Capacity is unchanged.
- **Core (`worker/utils.py`):** a 12-page block isn't a whole number of kernel pages from the next block, and padding it would grow every pool block to ≈4.3 MB.
  - Instead, `map_kv_cache_to_kernel_blocks` numbers kernel blocks in units of gcd(block stride, kernel block size).
  - Only specs that opt in with the new `kernel_block_alignment`, met by that unit, get this; the HiSparse indexer declares 16 B.
  - Other specs, including DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, keep the startup `ValueError`.
  - Whole-kernel-block layouts map as before, and kernel block ids are checked against the int32 range.
- Pure-MLA models keep one indexer page per block. GLM-5.3-NVFP4 groups are unchanged (all 64-token, 10.98× at 139k).

## Test Plan

`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` rev `eb9eb208`, TP4, bf16 KV, prefix caching, CUDA graphs:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --revision eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a \
  --trust-remote-code --language-model-only -tp 4 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":32}}'
```

- **GSM8K:** `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` prompts, 5-shot, greedy. 1319 questions at concurrency 32 (twice for HiSparse), then 200 at concurrency 1.
- **Long context from host:** 100-shot prompts (~16.9k tokens), 200 questions, `--max-model-len 18432 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4G`.
- **Capacity:** startup concurrency at `--max-model-len 139264 --max-num-seqs 256`.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k hisparse
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py
pytest tests/test_attention_backend_registry.py -k opt_in
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py -k hisparse
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py -k pooled_rows  # GPU
```

## Test Results

No errors or NaN responses in any run.

| Hardware | Variant | GSM8K | Long context from host |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4×B200 | no HiSparse, `main` | 0.911 / 0.911 / 0.923 ¹ | |
| 4×B200 | no HiSparse, this PR | 0.910 / 0.923 ¹ | 0.925 / 0.930 ² |
| 4×B200 | HiSparse | 0.916 / 0.914 / 0.935 | 0.935 / 0.935 (1,194 GB host→device, 41% hot misses) |
| 4×B200 | HiSparse, fp8 KV | 0.914 | |
| 4×B200 | HiSparse, KDA blocks at indexer page | 0.919, 0.940 (C=1) | 0.935 / 0.940; 0.930 (561 GB host→device, 44% hot misses) |
| 4×B200 | same, fp8 KV | 0.914 | |
| 4×H200 (FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE) | HiSparse | 0.918 / 0.917 / 0.925 | 0.945 / 0.915 (1,155 GB host→device, 41% hot misses) |

¹ Separate server runs. Greedy outputs differ between runs on `main` itself (36.6% identical, vs 35–40% for main vs this PR). ² Earlier revision of this PR.

Host traffic was read with the metrics interval lowered to 20 steps (local patch). The prefix-cache hit rate was 98.5% on B200 and 98.9% on H200.

**Capacity** (4×H200, bf16, max concurrency at 139k tokens)

| no HiSparse | HiSparse before | + hot/resident packing | + one indexer page per block | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 28.45 | 26.09 | 33.68 | 59.17 | **136.90** |

**Performance** (4×B200, fp8 KV, host pool 200 GiB; `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --seed 42`)

| Load | no HiSparse | one indexer page per block | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64k/2k, C=1: tok/s, TPOT | 174.0, 5.01 ms | 163.6, 5.38 ms | 162.5, 5.43 ms |
| 64k/2k, C=32: tok/s, TPOT | 985.3, 25.36 ms | 966.8, 25.98 ms | 971.0, 25.84 ms |
| 64k/16k, C=256: tok/s, TTFT, TPOT | 4309, 295 s, 29.1 ms | | 3835, **185 s**, 54.9 ms |
| 128k/16k, C=256: tok/s, TTFT, TPOT | 2707, 634 s, 29.1 ms | | **2756**, **384 s**, 68.2 ms |

At matched concurrency, multi-page indexer blocks add no per-step cost. At C=256 HiSparse runs every request at once (440.7× vs 117.5× concurrency at 64k, 251.6× vs 75.0× at 128k), so TPOT is higher.

**Unit tests:** each new test fails without its change. They cover:
- mirrors only inside connector steps;
- `supports_hisparse` opt-in;
- hot-group packing;
- indexer page sizing;
- unaligned packed kernel blocks, including their rejection without the opt-in and groups copied after binding;
- KDA blocks taking HiSparse's size;
- the int32 id range;
- the GPU kpool test, which passes on B200.

The V1 Attention CI jobs now also run when `kpool_compress.py` changes. The remaining Mac failures also occur on `main`.

Before this PR, an int `block_stride_alignment` only meant "pad the block stride to a multiple of N bytes". Here it also becomes permission for `map_kv_cache_to_kernel_blocks` to split blocks that are not a whole number of kernel pages apart: instead of raising the ValueError, it builds a view whose stride(0) is gcd(block stride, page size), i.e. smaller than a kernel page.
